Check the convergence of a fitted mixture model

convergence.Rd

Checks whether a fitted model reached a trustworthy maximum of the likelihood, with the checks Mplus reports for mixture models (computed by LatentMixtures.convergence in Julia):

Usage

convergence(object, newton = TRUE)

# S3 method for class 'lm_convergence'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted model from lca(), lpa(), lta() or growth() (including multigroup models).

newton

Logical; run check 3, which costs one Hessian of the log-likelihood.

x

An lm_convergence object.

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class lm_convergence: a list with ok (no problem found), converged, iterations, starts_converged, starts, replicated, ll, ll_newton, gradient, smallest_class, problems and notes (character vectors). Printing it shows the checks.

Details

  1. the best random start met the EM convergence criterion within maxiter;

  2. the best log-likelihood is replicated by at least two final-stage starts (otherwise the solution may be a local maximum: increase starts);

  3. with newton = TRUE, a few safeguarded Newton steps from the EM estimates raise the log-likelihood by less than 0.001 and the gradient there is close to zero, i.e. EM did not stop short of the maximum;

  4. the solution is not degenerate: no nearly singular growth-factor covariance matrix (GMM), no within-profile variance at zero (LPA). Item probabilities at 0 or 1 (LCA) and classes below 5% are reported as notes.

Checks 1, 2 and the growth-factor check also run automatically when a model is fitted and print a warning when they fail.

See also

fitstats() for the replication count in the fit statistics.

Examples

data(aces)
# \donttest{
# Is the 4-class ACE solution a trustworthy maximum of the likelihood?
m <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4)     # 4 ACE classes, as generated
#> Starting Julia ...
convergence(m)   # check that the best LL is replicated and EM reached the maximum
#> Convergence check: ✓ no problems found
#>   best start converged      yes (77 EM iterations)
#>   stage-2 starts converged  20 / 20
#>   best LL replicated        20 times
#>   LL at EM / after Newton   -5248.0073 / -5248.0073 (gain 0.0e+00; max |gradient| 1.4e-13)
#>   smallest class            0.099
#>   · EM converged; 1 Newton steps (polish = true) raised the log-likelihood by 5.5e-07 (max |gradient| 1.3e-03 → 3.3e-07); the reported solution is the Newton one
# if a check fails, refit with more random starts
if (!convergence(m)$ok) m <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4, starts = c(400, 80))
# }
